title: ASASSN-14ko flares were not weaker in 2022-2024 than in 2017-2021 while the period decrease slowed; a period change proportional to flare energy fails if the slowdown is real
abstract: Question: in repeating partial tidal disruption models of ASASSN-14ko, the orbit changes because the star loses mass at each passage, and the same mass powers the flare. If the period change per orbit is proportional to the radiated energy (hypothesis H_E), the slower period decrease after 2021 that prior studies found needs weaker flares. Approach: we measured the fluence, peak amplitude and shape of 16 well-sampled ASAS-SN g-band flares (2017-2024) and 7 Swift UVW2 flares (2020-2023), and the period change rate from peak times in two segments. Results: from 2017-2021 to 2022-2024 the g fluence ratio is 1.34 (95% interval 0.88-2.03; profile fit 1.64), the UVW2 fluence ratio is 1.49 (0.95-2.07), and the peak amplitude ratios are 0.89 and 0.99. Over the same eras dP/dn changed from -0.42 +/- 0.05 to -0.18 +/- 0.12 d per cycle (ratio 0.44). If the slowdown starts at cycles 21-24, H_E is rejected for all fluence proxies (p = 0.002-0.025). Fluence-weighted period clocks fit all peak times worse than a constant period derivative. The result depends on the break location: with a break at cycles 25-26, the slowdown itself is weak and H_E is not rejected; averaged over the break profile, p = 0.02-0.04 (UV) and 0.07-0.13 (g). The flare rise became slower (rise width 2.3 to 8.3 d), so the half-rise and peak markers drift apart by +7.5 d (4.2-10.9). The peak is the most stable timing marker, and its residuals do not correlate with flare shape. We also found that no public data (ASAS-SN, Swift, TESS, Rubin alerts) cover the 2026 flares yet. Limitations: aperture photometry, few flares per era, band-limited fluence, and an assumed single break.

display.caption: (a) The period of ASASSN-14ko decreased by 0.42 d per cycle in 2017-2021 and by 0.18 d per cycle after cycle 24. (b, c) The g-band and UVW2 flare fluence did not decrease; the gray band and dashed line show the level that a period change proportional to flare energy needs.
Monte Carlo distributions of the period-change ratio R_P (gray) and the energy ratio R_E (orange) between 2021-2026 and 2017-2021, with a break at cycle 24. H_E needs R_P = R_E.
p value of H_E for 72 variants per energy proxy (break cycle 21-26, two timing sets, removal of flare 25 or 28). Blue: segment A from cycle 11; green: from cycle 14, which has little power.
